name: v2 Comic panel, helmet on collar
medium: photographed panel from a newsprint comic book; head described as an object
prompt: Photograph of a single panel from a 1940s ten-cent war comic book, printed on yellowed newsprint, shot flat under warm lamp light. A figure in an olive drab greatcoat, leather gloves and canvas leggings stands at attention in front of a canvas tent. Where a head would be there is only a steel helmet: the helmet sits low, directly on the turned-up coat collar like a lid on a jar, and the whole opening between the helmet brim and the collar is printed as one flat solid black shape, pure black ink with a hard edge. Bold black brush outlines, flat four-colour inks, coarse visible halftone dots, olive, khaki, brick red and pale yellow. Empty white speech balloon above, paper grain, slight page curl.

name: v2 Ink cartoon, helmet on collar
medium: frontline one-panel gag cartoon; head described as an object
prompt: Single-panel 1940s frontline newspaper gag cartoon, black brush ink and grease crayon on rough off-white newsprint. A figure in a heavy wool overcoat sits on an ammunition crate in a muddy foxhole, squared to the viewer, thick gloves holding a tin cup. Where a head would be there is only a steel helmet resting directly on the turned-up overcoat collar, and the gap between the helmet brim and the collar is filled edge to edge with one flat pool of solid black ink. Heavy slashing brush strokes, deep spotted blacks, scratchy crayon tone on the mud and sky, sagging tired posture. Wide blank strip of paper below the drawing reserved for a typed caption. Slight ink bleed, visible paper fibre.

name: v2 Poster, helmet on collar
medium: wartime lithographic poster; head described as an object
prompt: 1940s wartime security poster, stone lithograph with flat silkscreen-like colour, printed on heavy cream paper with pinholes in the corners. A monumental figure seen from the chest up in an olive greatcoat with a tall collar raised, one gloved hand lifted with index finger upright. The head is a steel helmet in three flat tones resting directly on the raised collar, and the space between the helmet brim and the collar is one clean flat solid black shape, graphic and geometric, like a cut-out of black paper. Limited palette of olive, signal red, cream and black, soft airbrushed gradient in the background, strong diagonal composition, wide blank cream band along the bottom reserved for a slogan.

name: v2 Cel frame, helmet on collar
medium: 1940s Technicolor cel animation; head described as an object
prompt: Frame from a 1940s Technicolor theatrical cartoon, hand-inked cel over a painted gouache background. A tall figure in an olive greatcoat, gloves and boots stands in a night-time guard post under a single hanging lamp. The head is a steel helmet resting directly on the upturned greatcoat collar, and between the helmet brim and the collar the animators have painted one flat black shape with a hard edge. Dramatic low camera angle, art deco composition, long diagonal shadows. Clean dark ink outlines, flat cel colours with one hard-edged shadow tone. Painted background in deep teal, rust and amber with a soft airbrushed light cone, subtle cel dust and film grain, 4:3 frame.

name: v2 Caption box covers the head
medium: comic panel; the lettering box hides him
prompt: Photograph of a single panel from a 1940s ten-cent war comic book, printed on yellowed newsprint, shot flat under warm lamp light. A soldier in olive drab field jacket, leather gloves and canvas leggings stands at attention in front of a canvas tent, steel helmet on top. A large rectangular pale-yellow caption box with a black border has been pasted across the panel, overlapping the figure and covering everything from the helmet brim down to the jacket collar, so the helmet pokes out above the box and the shoulders continue below it. The caption box is blank. Bold black brush outlines, flat four-colour inks, coarse visible halftone dots, olive, khaki, brick red and pale yellow, paper grain, slight page curl.

name: v2 Censor block covers the head
medium: press photograph; the censor's block covers brim to collar
prompt: 1940s US Army Signal Corps press photograph, black-and-white silver gelatin print with white border, lying flat on a wooden desk. A soldier in wool greatcoat with the collar turned up, gloves and steel helmet sits upright on a folding chair in front of a tent, hands on knees. A military censor has painted one large tall block of opaque black ink on the print, brush edges visible, covering the whole area from the helmet brim down to the coat collar and from ear to ear, so only the helmet dome shows above the block. A purple ink stamp mark reading PASSED BY EXAMINER is stamped at an angle on the white border. Grease-pencil crop marks in the margin, soft window light.
